TRIAL OF THE PIRATES.


MONDAY, July 16, 1827.


The Circuit Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, Chief Justice Marshall, met pursuant to adjournment, at 9 o'clock, in the Hall of Delegates for the trial of Cuero, Pope, and Felix Barreto charged with murder and piracy aboard the Brigantine Crawford Capt. Brighman. Counsel for the United States, Barnard, District Attorney. For defendants, Leigh and Schmidt.


Mr. Adolph Crozet sworn in on the cross, as interpreter.


Mr. Schmidt, in behalf of the Prisoners, submitted two motions to the Court for change of venue, on account of the prejudices in the City of Richmond, produced by exaggerated newspaper representations of their guilt, and for continuance of the trial until the regular term of the Court in November next, that the Prisoners in the interim might be enabled to collect proofs of their character and standing in their native island of Cuba. The affidavit of the Prisoners upon which these two motions were founded, alleged the responsibility of the defendants to their own country, that their pecuniary situation placed them above the temptation of the crimes with which they were charged, and that their object going on board the Crawford, to visit the U. States, was commerce and speculation.


Before the Court determined these motions, the Prisoners were arraigned on the general charge of piracy and the issue made up on that charge, to which they respectively pleaded not guilty; they were then respectively arraigned on the murder of Brighman, Potter, Bicknell, and Deliver, to which arraignment, they also pleaded not guilty.
